thread.title: Stock Market Poised To End Losing Streak | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stock Market Poised To End Losing Streak | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market today was on track for the first gain in the major indexes in four sessions.
X Defensive plays — such as tobacco, medical care and utilities — led the gainers.
The Nasdaq advanced 0.6%, while the S&P 500 added 0.2%. The Dow Jones industrial average was just above flat. Small caps gained 0.2% on the Russell 2000.
Volume accelerated on both major exchanges vs. the previous session.
Apple ( AAPL ) bounced off its 10-week line near 220.83. The stock rose 1.2% in volume that at one point ran 55% above average.
The move to the 10-week line was Apple's first since a breakaway gap Aug. 1. That means the current action constitutes a buy opportunity .

Please contact customer service CLOSE The overall market uptrend's under-pressure label somewhat undermines stock purchases. Buys are more at more risk when an uptrend is under pressure but less risky than when the market is in correction.
Ideally, IBD-style investors prefer a strong uptrend in the general market . A market tailwind can help a stock succeed.
Gauging The Stock Market Pullback The Nasdaq has fallen about 6% in the current pullback. A pullback of 10% hasn't been suffered since March/April, when the index lost almost 11%. From that low, the Nasdaq rebounded 19.5% in about five months.
Elite stocks have struggled in the pullback. For example, the Innovator IBD 50 Fund ( FFTY ) dropped as much as 10.6% in this pullback. The exchange-traded fund was up 0.4% late Tuesday morning.
In the blue-chip Dow, gainers led losers by a narrow margin. Walmart ( WMT ) popped 2% in heavy volume. On the downside, heavy equipment maker Caterpillar ( CAT ) sagged 2% to test its 200-day moving average. Cat's volume also was heavy.
Two Breakouts Breakouts Tuesday included oilfield services provider Tidewater ( TDW ) and oil pipeline firm Kinder Morgan ( KMI ).
The balance of new highs and new lows continued to tilt negative. IBD's adjusted combined new lows outnumbered new highs 430-to-47 Monday. In Tuesday's action, preliminary data showed new lows holding their advantage.
